fd_install.source_fact: Installs the supplied struct file pointer into an FD table and consumes the file reference.

direct_close_path.source_fact: close(fd) removes the FD-table entry, calls filp_flush(), then calls __fput_sync(file) before returning to user space.

final_fput.source_fact: __fput_sync decrements the file reference count and calls __fput(file) inline only when that decrement reaches zero.

fsnotify_close.source_fact: For FMODE_OPENED files, __fput(file) calls fsnotify_close(file) before subsequent cleanup/free; the same struct file pointer is passed.
fsnotify_close.fanotify_mask_mapping: BUILD_BUG_ON asserts FAN_CLOSE_WRITE == FS_CLOSE_WRITE and FAN_CLOSE_NOWRITE == FS_CLOSE_NOWRITE

generic_fput.source_fact: The generic fput() path can queue ____fput as task_work or enqueue delayed work; direct SYSCALL_DEFINE1(close) instead calls __fput_sync.

fanotify_fid_name_merge.source_fact: Queued FID/name events with matching merge identity may merge, and fanotify_merge ORs the new event mask into the queued event.

design_implications: A source-pinned direct close profile may use close syscall exit as an upper-bound ordering marker only after an observer independently proves the matching final __fput occurred; close exit by itself remains insufficient.
A close error is not a reliable indication that the descriptor remains installed: sys_close clears it before flush and invokes __fput_sync afterward.

To preserve separate MODIFY and CLOSE_WRITE raw events under the current strict single-bit parser, the runtime design should persist a name-group EAGAIN barrier after the writer cgroup is empty and before the final close, then record the post-close drain separately. This prevents queued pre-close events from being merged with the close event only if no further writer events can occur after the barrier.

The barrier is a proposal for a future static contract review, not a runtime observation or guarantee; fanotify queue loss, event merge, target source/build mismatch, or missing trusted observer still makes the attempt incomplete.
